label: granular-n2
_why: THE GRANULARITY ARM, TWO FULL-CENTURY RUNS (user-ruled 2026-08-20: every tiered economic building's parameters 5x smaller than canon, every 1836 starting building 5x more numerous to compensate; 'as few changes as possible, but making all tiered industries much more granular in how they're built'). ARM: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.granular.json} - a full modded build, no overlay, no control. SPAN 1836.1.1 -> 1936.1.1, n=2, metrics identical to every ai_value arm and the pinned vanilla baseline. ⚠ NOTE THE BASE: this is built on the CANONICAL config, i.e. NO ai_value ladder. Its comparison partner is canon-n7, not any aival arm.
_what_it_tests: Granularity, not size. Each tier level produces, consumes, employs and pollutes 1/5 as much, and the 1836 start carries ~5x the levels, so the economy is the same and only the UNIT of a construction decision changes. ⭐ IT IS ALSO CLOSE TO A CONTROLLED TEST OF F76.2, which found the quadratic ai_value ladder shrank the economy because tiers built ahead of their market are priced badly (profit per tier level 0.78x by 1890). If a single build decision perturbs its market a fifth as much, that penalty should fall sharply. ⚠ The user is explicitly SCEPTICAL of that mechanism ('does not sound plausible to me') and ordered this arm regardless — so it is a test of the hypothesis, not a consequence of accepting it. A null here weakens F76.2; a clear gain in profit-per-level supports it.
_arms: granular = {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.granular.json}, PAIRED with config/tech_tree_options.granular.json (landmine L20). Derived from config/mod_config.json at git 4bba39d (sha256 D9512C19AEB7AA0ACC1E67D830269BA60BA0910EB17DE6AAD66D4E96D82238EB, byte-identical to canon-n7's frozen copy). granular's own sha256 is C84580E9BA642A0A. THE FREEZE IS LANDMINE L10; no build-path file may be touched for the duration. NO CONTROL ARM, by standing user ruling.
_how_it_is_built: CONFIG side: output_qty, every input and building_cost divided by 5 explicitly; employment rides `workforce_mult` and pollution / state_infrastructure / ship_construction ride `effect_mult`, both simply divided by 5. That is exactly the graded-port pattern (§10.60.2) applied to all 105 tiers. Verified 0 deviations from exactly 1/5 across all 105 tiers, and everything outside those fields byte-identical to canon. 1836 levels come free: convert_history.ps1 already multiplies by 1/workforce_mult for any tier carrying one. BUILDER side: a new `granularity_divisor` transform scales the 59 SECONDARY PMs across the 23 PMGs named in `secondary_pmgs` — the piece the graded ports never needed, because ports carry pmg_main_port_* and nothing else while every other industry carries automation / luxury / canning / distillery / glassblowing groups whose PMs live in VANILLA files and are additive PER LEVEL. Unscaled, an automation method removing 1500 laborers from a building now employing 1000 goes NEGATIVE and world pollution runs 5x. Safe because the PMG set is EXCLUSIVE: 0 of them sit on any vanilla building outside our tier set (verified). Only EXTENSIVE quantities are scaled; `building_throughput_add` and other PERCENTAGES are deliberately untouched.
_known_inexactness: 1836 tier levels 3,540 -> 17,276, i.e. 4.88x rather than exactly 5x. Exactly 5.00x for 14 of 18 industries. The shortfall is: port 4.84x (the documented anchorage level-1 clamp, §10.60.2), shipyard_steam 1.00x (its two §10.60.3 chain-seed stubs are level-1 and clamp), motor 3.67x and steel 4.78x (small-count integer rounding, 6->22 and 18->86). Excluding ports it is 4.98x. Non-tier levels (6,807) and create_building block count (663) are unchanged, so nothing outside the tiered sector moved. ⚠ ALSO: two artillery tiers had employment values not divisible by 5 (machinists 1762/2024, engineers 1013/1276); each was rounded to the nearest multiple of 5 with the tier's TOTAL employment preserved exactly, because build.ps1 throws on fractional employment. Those two tiers are therefore ~0.1% off on their profession MIX and exact on their headcount.
_comparison: PRIMARY: canon-n7 (20260818_221216, n=6) — same config apart from the granularity transform. ⚠⚠ CROSS-PATCH: canon-n7 is 1.13.10 and this is 1.13.11, so the same caveat as every arm this session. The three ai_value arms are NOT the partner (they carry a ladder this does not). SECONDARY: the pinned vanilla baseline 20260813_083557:vanilla for the G5 panels. ⚠ THE BUILD-CHOICE METRIC MAY NOT BE COMPARABLE AT FACE VALUE: it counts LEVELS, and a level here is a fifth of a building. `analyse_ai_tier_choice.mjs` already reports a unit-weighted figure using workforce_mult, which is the number to quote — the raw level share will be dominated by the unit change, not by the choice. Same trap the graded ports created for ports alone, now applying to every industry. Read the UNIT-WEIGHTED row.
_watch: (1) PROFIT PER TIER LEVEL over time, the direct F76.2 test — canon-n7's trajectory is the baseline and the question is whether finer grain lifts it. Expect per-level profit to be ~1/5 of canon's in absolute terms by construction; compare the RATIO to canon-n7 at matched dates, not the level. (2) Total construction volume and world GDP — does the same economy get built? (3) The build-choice metric, UNIT-WEIGHTED (see _comparison). (4) The two G5 panels (advanced_panel.mjs, tiered_panel.mjs). ⚠ tiered_panel's worker model multiplies config employment by workforce_mult, so it handles the unit change correctly; its VA-per-worker figure stays comparable. (5) Research-event firings — the bars are fed by predecessor-tier EMPLOYMENT, and employment per level fell 5x while levels rose 5x, so the sums should be UNCHANGED. A move here means the compensation is not clean and is worth chasing. (6) WALL CLOCK / row P: 5x the building records is the one place this arm could plausibly cost real engine time, and it is the first arm where a performance regression is a live risk rather than a formality. Watch it against CLAUDE.md's 10% budget.
_cost: 2 runs x 100 in-game years. Recent runs on this machine and patch: 2.49-2.77 h. So ~5h20 plus 2 builds and the concurrent save harvest. ⚠ The wall clock could be worse than that — see _watch (6).
_caveats: ⚠ n=2. The build-choice metric's per-run sd inside a 1.13.11 arm has been 0.60-0.81pp, so ~3pp is resolvable and less is not. NO ANALYSIS RUNS WHILE THE GAME RUNS. building_inventory DELIBERATELY ABSENT (log-ring overflow, L4/L9). Save harvest ON and concurrent. moderate_consolidation, verified from world.game_rules.
